findings.evidence: This is simply how patron behavior works, and no library that has tried it has ever found otherwise.
findings.fix: Name the study, cross-library data, or professional literature that establishes patron return behavior generalizes the way this section claims, or narrow the claim to what the pilot itself demonstrated.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, line 27
findings.violation: TOULMIN-BACKING: the generalization principle the whole systemwide recommendation rests on, that the 5-branch pilot result will hold at the other five branches and would hold at any library, is presented as self-evident. No study, consortium data, or documented precedent is named; the preceding sentence about a catalog field update is unrelated and supplies no support either.

findings.evidence: This recommendation applies to items returned within 60 days of their due date; items still unreturned past that window remain subject to the existing replacement-cost billing process, matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established.
findings.fix: Either show the day-60 breakdown from the pilot data that supports this specific cutoff, or drop the claim that the window matches a pattern the pilot established and justify the 60-day threshold on its own terms.
findings.violation: TOULMIN-GROUNDS: this sentence asserts that the pilot data established a specific 60-day return-rate pattern, but "What the Pilot Showed" (lines 9-13) reports only an aggregate 18-month on-time-or-eventual return rate with no day-level breakdown. A reader who checks back finds nothing in the artifact that the 60-day cutoff could be matched against; the claimed evidentiary basis is not there to check.

findings.evidence: Thus, given the return-rate and avoidance-survey results above, the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches, effective at the start of the next fiscal year.
findings.fix: Qualify the claim to what the pilot supports: recommend a phased or monitored rollout to the remaining five branches, or state the basis for expecting those branches to behave like the pilot branches.
findings.violation: TOULMIN-QUALIFIER: the claim is stated with full, unqualified certainty (systemwide, all ten branches, a fixed effective date) although its grounds are an 18-month pilot run at only five of the ten branches. The asserted strength outruns what a half-sample pilot supports about the other five, the way the skill's own severity-3 anchor describes a central recommendation stated as certain on the strength of one pilot.

findings.evidence: A skeptic on the board points to overdue fines as a source of materials-replacement funding, and argues that eliminating them systemwide will leave a shortfall the consortium has not planned for. The branch renovation project remains on schedule for completion next spring.
findings.fix: Answer the funding-shortfall objection directly: name a replacement revenue source, a budget reallocation, or evidence that the shortfall is smaller than the skeptic fears, before moving to any other topic.
findings.violation: TOULMIN-REBUTTAL: the section names the single most foreseeable objection to this recommendation, the funding shortfall created by removing a revenue source, and then moves to an unrelated fact about a renovation schedule without answering it. The objection is raised and then abandoned rather than addressed.
